title: Choose the visual world for the Hibiki site
question: The roll assigned The Battle Map. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Battle Map
options.lineage: the gridded battle map under the table lamp, and the VTT's ambient-sound radii drawn on it
options.thesis: The landing page is one map; sound sources are glowing radii on the grid, and Hibiki is what lights them.
options.viewport: Full-bleed dark grid. Three overlapping sound radii (amber music, teal ambience, rose effects) breathe around a party token at the centre; the title and one-line pitch sit top-left on the map, Download for macOS/Windows/Linux as the single framed object beneath. The real Cozy Tavern scene board floats as a window at the right edge, labelled as an illustration.
options.risk: A grid on dark can slide toward a technical dashboard if the lines are cold or the type is small; warmth has to come from the lamp light and the lettering.

raised.raise: One orchestrated motion: the three radii light in sequence on load and then breathe at their own tempo, like real level meters, instead of scattered hover effects.
Saturated colour only where it matters now: the three radii own the colour; everything else is charcoal ink, and hierarchy comes from field size and colour, not type weight.
One continuous ground: every section is a region on the same map, no boxed cards, the grid runs under the whole page.
The download is staged as the one framed object on the page; secondary actions recede into plain ink links.
A fast version in the corner: a three-line quick start for people who refuse to read the setup walkthrough.

options.label: The DM Screen
options.lineage: the four-panel folding GM screen: art facing the players, reference tables facing the GM
options.thesis: Two faces of one object: the players' side is the mascot art, the GM's side is the setup tables.
options.viewport: A wide folded screen spanning the viewport: left panels carry the campfire art and the pitch, right panels carry download and the setup checklist as reference tables.
options.risk: Familiar: dark panels with reference tables is where most landing pages in this category land, and the folded conceit can read as decoration.

options.label: VU-Meter Bridge
options.lineage: a row of ballistic VU needles across a recording desk
options.thesis: Hibiki as a desk: one meter per layer, all leaning into the downbeat together.
options.viewport: A bridge of three meters (music, ambience, effects) across the top, needles moving to the real scene; download beneath the desk edge.
options.case: Wins product clarity (sound layers as channels) but GMs do not identify with a studio desk; the brand explicitly refuses the recording-studio feel.
options.risk: Reads as pro-audio gear, not a game table.

options.label: Glazier's Colourfield Partition
options.lineage: a steel-framed glass partition, mostly clear with a few saturated panes
options.thesis: The soundboard as a glazing grid: one pane, one statement, colour only where it plays.
options.viewport: A wall elevation of panes read left to right; the scene board is the lit section, download a single amber pane.
options.case: Strong clarity through the pane grid, weak audience identification: nobody at a game table thinks in glazing.
options.risk: Could read as a generic bento layout.

options.label: Ebru Floated Pigment
options.lineage: pigment combed on a water bath and lifted in one contact
options.thesis: Sound layers as pigment displacing on one surface.
options.viewport: A full-frame fluid canvas with the title lifted off it.
options.case: Beautiful but tells a GM nothing about what Hibiki does.
options.kept: Everything on one continuous ground, no stacked boxes.

options.label: Deco Cinema Lobby
options.lineage: an Art Deco cinema lobby at premiere hour
options.thesis: Arrival staged as marquee, lobby, house.
options.viewport: A sunburst marquee with the name climbing stepped tiers.
options.case: Loses both axes: not the audience's world, and the staging hides the product.
options.kept: The primary action gets the one framed treatment; secondaries recede.

options.label: Wildstyle Blackbook Page
options.lineage: a writer's blackbook with interlocked letters and a fast throw-up in the corner
options.viewport: The word HIBIKI interlocked across the page.
options.case: Loses both axes for a TTRPG audience and buries the download.
options.kept: A fast version sketched in the corner: the three-line quick start.

options.label: Versailles Bosquet Vistas
options.lineage: axial garden vistas and hidden green rooms
options.thesis: The page as one sightline that reveals rooms.
options.viewport: A long central axis from terrace to canal.
options.kept: One reading axis: a single column aligned to the grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark landing page: mascot banner hero, three feature cards, download buttons, setup steps, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Banner, headline, two buttons, a row of cards.
canonCard.risk: What the site already is, just tidier.
